points, sliding linear regression
Baseline F0
Mean of the first N readings in the time window (after blank subtraction). SD is the standard deviation of those N readings.
Fmax / Tmax
Maximum of the (smoothed) curve and the time it occurs; ΔF = Fmax − F0, fold = Fmax / F0.
Threshold & call
A curve crosses the threshold when n consecutive readings are ≥ the threshold; the crossing time is interpolated linearly between neighbouring points. Readings above the threshold at the very end of a run that are fewer than n do not count. Wells that cross before the cut-off time with ΔF > 0 are positive. “Negative-control mean + k×SD” uses all readings of the negative-control group. With “baseline + k×SD”, a baseline whose readings are all identical (SD = 0) is given the rounding noise of the readings instead (smallest step ÷ √12).
Lag time
Threshold = time the threshold is crossed (time to threshold); amplitude % = first time F0 + p%·ΔF is reached; tangent = the max-slope tangent meeting F = F0, t_lag = t_ms − (F_ms − F0) / k_max; sigmoid fit F = A1 + (A2 − A1) / (1 + e^((t½ − t)/τ)) (Levenberg–Marquardt), lag time = t½ − 2τ, apparent rate k = 1/τ.
1/lag time
Reciprocal of the lag time, usable as a rate (called RAF in some papers). A well that did not rise counts as 0, so the mean of a group includes every valid well.
Wells that do not rise
A negative well has no lag time, T50 or time to plateau: all that is known is that they are later than the end of its run (the end of the time window, or the cut-off time). In the group statistics the mean uses only the wells that rose and shows their number; the “Median” counts the others as later than the end and reads “> end time” when half of the wells or more did not rise. Between groups, the t-test compares only the wells that rose, the Mann–Whitney test ranks the others last, and Fisher’s exact test compares the numbers of positive wells.
T50
First time the curve reaches F0 + ½ΔF (or ½ Fmax), interpolated linearly.
Time to plateau
Time the curve enters its plateau. Default = first sustained time at F0 + 90%·ΔF; tangent = the max-slope tangent meeting F = Fmax, t = t_ms + (Fmax − F_ms) / k_max; fit = t½ + 2τ, not reported when it lies after the last reading (the plateau was not observed). The instant of the maximum reading jumps around on a noisy plateau and does not mark plateau entry; it is hidden by default (tick it under “Columns…”).
Max slope
dF/dt from a sliding linear regression over w points of the smoothed curve; the maximum is reported with its time and signal.
Group positive
A group (sample) is positive when the share of positive replicates is ≥ the setting (default 50%, e.g. ≥ 2 of 4 wells).
AUC
Trapezoidal integral over the time window; with baseline removal it integrates F − F0. Units: signal × time.
